title: Lemmings Don't Jump Off Cliffs. A 1958 Film Staged the Scene
subject: lemming

scenes.text: Lemmings don't jump off cliffs. So who threw them?
The famous scene comes from a 1958 Disney film called White Wilderness. It showed lemmings leaping into the sea.
A 1983 Canadian investigation found the crew filmed in Alberta, where lemmings don't even live, and pushed the animals over the edge.
The sea was a river. Tight camera angles did the rest.
Real lemmings boom roughly tenfold every three to five years, then spread out to find food.
Some swim lakes and drown by accident. The suicide myth was a film trick.

description:
Lemmings don't commit mass suicide. The famous cliff scene was staged for a 1958 Disney film.
A 1983 Canadian investigation found the crew filmed in Alberta and pushed the animals over the edge, while real lemmings just spread out when their numbers boom.
Which animal myth fooled you the longest?
